title: Silverport AI - Implementation Kickoff & Runtime Intake
summary: Kickoff to align on Silverport's production inference requirements, network/VPC constraints, and pilot success criteria. Covered deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private), initial throughput/latency targets, and security needs (KMS, audit logs, SSO). Decided next: run a short synthetic benchmark, exchange security pack, and schedule a Dedicated sizing review with infra team.
topics: Current infra and constraints (VPC, egress, KMS)
Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: alright good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. This is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. quick roll call?
[00:08] Carlos: hi this is carlos, CTO at Silverport.
[00:11] Priya: priya here, platform engineering.
[00:13] Liam: liam, ml infra.
[00:15] Maya: maya, i'm the solutions engineer from redwood.
[00:18] Avery: avery in customer success, i'll be your onboarding lead.
[00:22] Jordan: great thanks. objective for today is to get an implementation intake, understand constraints and agree pilot success criteria, timeline and immediate actions.
[00:35] Carlos: yeah we want to get inference into production for our summarization pipeline by q3, primary concerns are latency and data residency, also SOC2 and k-m-s.
[00:48] Priya: to add, our infra sits in aws eu-west-1, we have strict egress rules, and all keys go through our HSM.
[00:56] Maya: okay makes sense. just to confirm, you mentioned k-m-s/hsm - we support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated, and hosted has bring-your-own-key options via a proxy, there may be some network setup for that though.
[01:12] Liam: what's the difference in latency between hosted and dedicated? we have a 150ms P95 budget per request for short summaries.
[01:20] Jordan: good question. typical hosted latencies for our curated models are in the 60-200ms P95 ballpark depending on sequence length and request pattern; dedicated gives you more predictable tails and throughput. for your use-case i'd tentatively recommend Dedicated, but we should run a small benchmark.
[01:40] Carlos: mm-hm ok. cost is also a factor — Dedicated commit costs are a concern for us.
[01:45] Maya: totally, there's a tradeoff. we can suggest a temporary burst/scale policy for the pilot to keep commit smaller and validate traffic patterns. also Redwood Optimize can give batching and quantization recs to reduce unit cost.
[02:02] Priya: we do a lot of short requests — users hit the API with short sequences. batch sizes will be small.
[02:10] Maya: that's helpful — small prefix, lots of concurrent requests. that'll favor lower-latency configs and aggressive KV-cache prefixing. note: our transcriber sometimes writes K-V cache as just K-V or KV, so docs vary.
[02:27] Liam: side question: can we pin model versions and do canary rollouts?
[02:31] Jordan: yes, rollouts (canary / A-B) are supported. you can pin model versions and set fallback policies to a smaller quantized model if SLOs slip.
[02:40] Emily: on security, we need audit logs to be immutable and to ship to our central splunk cluster. is that supported?
[02:48] Avery: yes audit logs and event streaming to customer endpoints is part of Private and Dedicated offerings. for hosted we can provide audit exports to a secure S3 bucket or a pub/sub endpoint.
[03:02] Carlos: we need ISO and SOC2 docs before procurement moves forward.
[03:06] Jordan: we'll share the security pack after the call — SOC2 type 2 report, encryption at rest/in transit, SSO/SAML guides.
[03:15] Priya: network — we are a no-egress policy, so Private or a VPC-peered Dedicated is the direction. how long does peering usually take?
[03:27] Maya: depends on networking teams but typical peering setup with our infra and customer's VPC is 2-5 business days if nothing unexpected; sometimes internal firewall rules take longer. we'll send a checklist for the networking intake.
[03:42] Liam: about the benchmark — what do you need from us to run a synthetic throughput/latency test?
[03:48] Jordan: ideally: representative prompt set (5-10k requests or a smaller sample), sequence length distribution, concurrency target, and a small test account or API key; we can run a single model type to baseline hosted vs dedicated.
[04:05] Carlos: we can provide a 2k sample set and a staging VPC.
[04:09] Jordan: perfect. we'll run baseline tests on hosted firstly, then propose a Dedicated sizing doc.
[04:16] Maya: note — quantized variants can change latency characteristics; we'll include guidance on 8-bit vs 4-bit and tradeoffs on quality. also mention: some of the ops docs call our private offering 'Private CP' which is shorthand in internal notes, so you'll see different naming.
[04:33] Priya: observability question — do we get token-level cost and latency for each route?
[04:37] Jordan: yes Redwood Console exposes per-route token cost, token counts, latency histograms and tracing hooks. for Dedicated we can push more retention, and for Private we can host the console or forward metrics to your datadog.
[04:50] Priya: got it.
[04:53] Carlos: timeline — we have procurement freeze on the 20th of april, can we get security docs and a rough pilot quote before then?
[05:02] Jordan: yes we'll prioritize that. quote + security pack by EOD next tuesday.
[05:08] Emily: two more quick items: SSO SAML integration - our idp is okta, and data residency — logs must stay in eu-west-1.
[05:18] Maya: okta is supported, we have a standard SAML guide. for logs retention and residency we can configure region-scoped storage for Dedicated/Private; for hosted we'll need to ensure endpoints and storage are region-bound.
[05:33] Liam: about model onboarding — we plan to fine-tune a small 7B model in house. can Redwood serve custom fine-tuned models?
[05:42] Jordan: yes, we can serve customer-supplied models in Dedicated and Private. hosted model uploads are possible via a managed onboarding path but have extra review. for the pilot Dedicated with an onboarding lane is the fastest.
[05:58] Carlos: ok that helps.
[06:01] Priya: sample infra diagram would help — how the VPC peering, subnets, and routing look with Redwood Dedicated.
[06:08] Avery: we'll attach a reference architecture diagram in the follow-up email.
[06:12] Maya: small gotcha from past customers — firewall teams sometimes block ephemeral egress IPs used for benchmarking; recommend opening a temporary CIDR which we will provide.
[06:25] Liam: noted.
[06:27] Jordan: any blockers on the integration side?
[06:29] Priya: only that we need procurement + security sign-off. once we get the SOC2 and KMS flow documented we'll be unblocked.
[06:38] Carlos: ok let's recap next steps.
[06:41] Jordan: recap: (1) Redwood to send security pack and SOC2 artifacts (Jordan) — target tuesday EOD. (2) Customer to provide sample prompt set and staging VPC details (Carlos/Priya) — target friday. (3) Redwood to run hosted baseline and share benchmark results and Dedicated sizing proposal (Maya/Jordan) — target following week. (4) Schedule Dedicated sizing call with infra (Avery to coordinate).
[07:09] Emily: can i get contact for compliance person?
[07:12] Jordan: yes i'll include our compliance lead in the follow-up thread.
[07:17] Carlos: excellent thanks everyone.
[07:20] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up with the pack and calendar invites.
[07:24] END TRANSCRIPT

Note: transcription contains occasional label swaps and minor word errors; timestamps are approximate and intended to segment the conversation.
